# Kumārapetavatthu (Pv 41)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Prince

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kumārapetavatthu* (Pv 41), translated as *The Prince*, is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. The text illustrates the karmic retributions of indulging in excessive sensual pleasures and committing adultery, showing how such deeds lead to torment and rebirth as a ghost (*peta*) [SuttaCentral; Law 1926; Clark 1994].

Scholars of Buddhist monastic literature have noted thematic and textual connections between this story and other traditions. In his study and edition of the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravādin *Abhisamācārikā Dharmāḥ*, Seishi Karashima observes verses in that Sanskrit Vinaya text that parallel or closely resemble verses found in the *Kumārapetavatthu* (specifically verse Pv 453, beginning *ayaṁ kumāro sīvathikāya chaḍḍito*) [Karashima 2012]. Modern comparative studies by Bimala Churn Law and Robert Warren Clark also cite the account of Kumārapeta as a prominent exemplar of the narrative motif wherein sexual misconduct results in severe post-mortem suffering [Law 1926; Clark 1994].

While SuttaCentral does not catalog curated parallels for the text, DharmaNexus identifies significant internal Pali text reuse [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, shares extensive text with the *Kumārapetavatthu* (8 matching segments, with §0.3–7.6 corresponding closely to commentary sections) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus detects shared verse passages between the *Kumārapetavatthu* (§§7.1–8.1) and the immediately following text in the collection, the *Rājaputtapetavatthu* (Pv 42, §§11.4–14.1) [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a) (§0.3–7.6 ↔ §2893–2913); Rājaputtapetavatthu (Pv 42) (§7.1–8.1 ↔ §11.4–14.1)
